x-m-el-sta-06.title: Choosing Sample Size Between Margin of Error and Budget
x-m-el-sta-06.goal: Find sample size meeting margin-of-error and budget conditions, separate problems bigger sample no fix.
x-m-el-sta-06.material: You wan estimate average daily smartphone minutes for school students using sample. Population standard deviation known 20 minutes, and when estimate population mean using sample mean, margin error (about 95% confidence)=2×20÷√n minutes (n sample size). Survey one person cost 3000원, budget 360000원.
x-m-el-sta-06.thinking.0: Find several answers meeting both conditions together
x-m-el-sta-06.thinking.1: Read relationship sample size and margin error
x-m-el-sta-06.thinking.2: Separate problems size solve from those it can't
x-m-el-sta-06.prereq.0: Meaning of sample mean, population mean and margin error
x-m-el-sta-06.prereq.1: Read formula and change to inequality (grade 10)
x-m-el-sta-06.s.s1.prompt: Find 3 different sample sizes n where margin error no more than 4 minutes and budget no exceed.
x-m-el-sta-06.s.s1.hint.0: First check margin error and cost when n=100.
x-m-el-sta-06.s.s1.hint.1: Compare how margin and cost change as n grow; find both ends of range.
x-m-el-sta-06.s.s1.fail.c1: Sample size must integer at least 1.
x-m-el-sta-06.s.s1.explain: For 40÷√n≤4, need √n≥10, so n≥100; budget says n≤120. Therefore any integer from 100 to 120 works.
x-m-el-sta-06.s.s2.prompt: Surveyor increase sample size from 100 to 400 and say, 'Now estimate no fit be wrong.' Which evaluation fit best?
x-m-el-sta-06.s.s2.hint.0: Put n=100 and n=400 into formula and compare error margins.
x-m-el-sta-06.s.s2.hint.1: Separate wetin bigger sample size reduce from wetin e no fit reduce.
x-m-el-sta-06.s.s2.o.a: Correct. With 400 people, sample mean go equal population mean no matter how dem choose sample.
x-m-el-sta-06.s.s2.r.a: Even if sample bigger, sample mean no become exactly population mean. More so if sample selection biased.
x-m-el-sta-06.s.s2.o.b: Error margin cut in half, but if dem choose sample with bias, bias still dey.
x-m-el-sta-06.s.s2.r.b: You separate error wey sample size reduce from bias wey come from how dem choose sample.
x-m-el-sta-06.s.s2.o.c: Wrong. Increasing sample size no reduce error margin at all.
x-m-el-sta-06.s.s2.r.c: For formula, when n bigger, 40÷√n smaller. Put n=100 and n=400 yourself, compare.
x-m-el-sta-06.s.s2.o.d: Error margin become one quarter, so estimate hardly fit be wrong.
x-m-el-sta-06.s.s2.r.d: When n become 4 times bigger, √n become 2 times bigger, so error margin no become one quarter. Put numbers and check.
x-m-el-sta-06.s.s2.explain: When n go from 100 to 400, wey na 4 times bigger, √n become 2 times bigger, so error margin cut in half, from 4 minutes to 2 minutes. Even so, bias from how dem choose sample no disappear when sample size increase.
